verdict.rationale: Cua documents a natural-language workflow: install Cua Driver once, add it to an agent such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, then ask that agent to do things in your apps through MCP or the CLI. The language understanding itself comes from third-party agents rather than a first-party conversational interface. A hands-on community report of the older cua-agent Gradio loop shows it acting on a task but typing in the wrong place and then failing to connect on two later runs. missing for 10: a first-party natural-language interface for operating Cua itself (Spaces, SDK, Bench), documentation of natural-language command coverage, and independent corroboration that natural-language tasks complete reliably.
